title: NovaHealth POC scoping - open models
next_steps: Redwood to run baseline latency + quality benchmark on customer's 2k eval prompts (due 2027-04-15)
Customer to share sample dataset and scoring rubric (by 2027-04-12)
Schedule in-depth security review with security team (proposed 2027-04-20)
Send pricing/commit options for Dedicated and Hosted POC (by 2027-04-13)
action_items: Priya - share benchmark plan and infra spec by EOD 2027-04-09
Elena - upload 2k evaluation prompts and 200 sample patient de-identified records by 2027-04-12
Diego - prepare shortlist of 3 model variants and quantization configs by 2027-04-13
summary: POC scoping call to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and open-model shortlist for NovaHealth's clinical summarization and triage assistant. Customer has strict PHI constraints, wants latency <200ms p95 for short summaries and strong multilingual support (EN/ES). Agreed 4-week POC split into benchmarking + integration. Redwood to run benchmarks on customer's eval set and propose top 3 open-model variants with quantization and hosting recommendations.
transcript:
[00:00] Priya Raman: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Priya, AE at Redwood. Diego from our SE team will lead the model/benchmark parts.
[00:12] Elena Park: Hi, Elena here. Head of ML at NovaHealth. Jonas and Maya with me.
[00:18] Jonas Reed: morning, thanks.
[00:20] Maya Patel: hello.
[00:22] Diego Morales: great, thanks. quick agenda: align success criteria, get workload numbers, agree benchmark plan, shortlist open models and timeline.
[00:35] Elena Park: high level - we're building a clinical summarization + triage assistant. Input is short clinical notes and patient messages, output is a 2-3 sentence summary and triage flag (urgent/non-urgent) and sometimes a suggested next action. we need high precision for triage, hallucinations are a big no.
[00:55] Priya Raman: understood. can you quantify the volume?
[00:58] Jonas Reed: for phase 1, it's about 150k requests/month, avg request token in/out around 300 tokens. latency goal is p95 < 200ms for the short summaries, throughput ~100-150 qps at peak. cost target: ideally keep hosted cost under $X per 1M tokens - (note: placeholder) - but we care more about latency and safety.
[01:25] Diego Morales: 150k/mo at 300 tokens - ok that's moderate. our POC can run on hosted or dedicated; given PHI concerns you mentioned, Maya, are you okay with Redwood hosted or prefer Private/VPC?
[01:39] Maya Patel: privacy is sensitive. we can start with hosted if we can get SOC2 Type II, audit logs, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys. otherwise we'll need VPC or Private runtime.
[01:54] Priya Raman: we can provide SOC 2, SAML SSO, audit logs, and KMS options - we'll share the security pack. for POC most customers go hosted with dedicated capacity to match latency SLOs.
[02:07] Elena Park: timeline? we want results quickly - ideally 3-4 weeks to pick a model and run a light pilot.
[02:14] Diego Morales: that's reasonable. propose 2-week benchmark + 2-week integration and small pilot. during benchmark we'll test accuracy on your 2k eval prompts, measure p95 latency, throughput, cost.
[02:26] Jonas Reed: what metrics for accuracy? triage precision/recall, summary ROUGE?
[02:30] Elena Park: triage F1 is primary, hallucination rate second, then summary faithfulness (we use a human score rubric).
[02:37] Diego Morales: perfect. for open-model shortlist, based on multilingual needs (EN/ES) and medical domain, our initial picks are: Llama-3-13B-instruct (quantized), Mistral-7B-instruct (recent medical finetune), Falcon-40B-instruct-qlora, and an opt-in smaller Med-specific model if you can share data. we'll rank by quality vs latency.
[02:58] Maya Patel: quick question - are those all available for hosted inference and can we quantize?
[03:03] Priya Raman: yes, hosted supports these; we can run int8 or int4 quantization in many cases, and we do continuous batching + KV cache to bring down costs. Diego will propose kernel/runtime configs.
[03:15] Elena Park: we've had better hallucination handling with closed models in the past, but we want to avoid vendor lock-in. open-models are preferred if quality is good enough.
[03:27] Diego Morales: understood. tradeoffs - bigger models (e.g., Falcon-40B) may give better factuality but cost and latency go up; 13B class models with instruction finetune + med-domain prompts often hit sweet spot for latency and quality. quantization can change hallucination patterns, so we'll test both accuracy and hallucination.
[03:47] Jonas Reed: what about multilingual (Spanish)? any model recommendations?
[03:50] Diego Morales: Llama-3-instruct has decent Spanish for summarization, Mistral variants are improving; we'll include bilingual prompts in the eval. if Spanish coverage is primary, we might include a multilingual model like Mosaic or a Spanish-specialized finetune.
[04:05] Elena Park: ok. workload sizing - for benchmarks, what infra do you need from us?
[04:09] Diego Morales: a de-identified sample dataset (200 de-identified patient notes and 2k evaluation prompts), plus an anonymized traffic pattern (peak qps, avg tokens) and acceptance rubric. credentials for a short-lived S3 bucket or secure share for the data.
[04:24] Maya Patel: we'll provide de-identified data via secure S3 and a short rubric. Our legal team needs minimal access and a DPIA statement.
[04:31] Priya Raman: we'll send the security pack and a short scope doc for the POC, including data handling and retention.
[04:36] Diego Morales: benchmark plan: phase A (week 1-2) - run 6 model variants across your eval set: Llama-3-13B-instruct (q4_int8 and q5_0), Mistral-7B-med-ft (q4), Falcon-40B-22b-instruct (q4), and a Med-tuned 7B variant. Collect triage F1, hallucination rate (manual + automatic checks), p95 latency on our hosted Dedicated config and on a Private small cluster. Phase B (week 3-4) - integrate top model in a canary route with 1% traffic and run live checks.
[05:12] Jonas Reed: sounds good. how do you measure hallucinations automatically?
[05:16] Diego Morales: we run entity overlap checks, contradiction detection, and sample manual review. also use retrieval augmentation tests to see if model pulls unsupported facts. we'll show flagged cases so you can judge tolerances.
[05:29] Elena Park: benchmarks need to mirror clinical phrasing and Spanish samples. Also need token-level cost estimates per 1M tokens for each config.
[05:37] Priya Raman: we'll include cost estimates, and Diego will provide latency/cost tradeoff curves.
[05:41] Maya Patel: if POC shows PHI risk or audit issues, we'd escalate to Private deployment - what are timeline differences?
[05:48] Priya Raman: Private deployment typically adds 3-4 weeks for network setup and KMS/HSM integration, so for POC we usually keep hosted but with customer-managed keys and contractual controls.
[05:59] Diego Morales: on model selection, the shortlist we'll test: Llama-3-13B-instruct (2 quant configs), Mistral-7B-med-ft (unquant and q4), Falcon-40B-instruct-qlora (q4), and a Med-7B tuned model. We'll add an extra multilingual candidate if NovaHealth wants stronger Spanish.
[06:20] Elena Park: can you also include a smaller low-latency model for edge cases?
[06:24] Diego Morales: yes, we'll include a 3B-class model as a fallback for sub-50ms local completions, though quality will be lower.
[06:31] Jonas Reed: what's the expected infra for hitting 150 qps with p95 <200ms?
[06:35] Diego Morales: parameter dependent. For 13B quantized on our Dedicated instances we can get p95 ~120-180ms at 150 qps with batching and optimized kernels. For 40B models you'd need more GPUs and latency likely increases; we'll provide concrete instance counts in the infra spec.
[06:54] Elena Park: success criteria recap - triage F1 >= 0.9 preferred, hallucination rate below 2% on eval set, p95 latency <200ms, and cost target TBD but we want to compare per-token cost across configs. If we meet these, we'll expand to 10k users.
[07:13] Priya Raman: great. timeline recap: Redwood runs benchmarks (week of Apr 12), deliver results and recommended model + quantization configs by Apr 15, then integration and small pilot Apr 18-29. we'll schedule security review Apr 20.
[07:30] Maya Patel: legal will need redlines for data retention and liability.
[07:34] Priya Raman: noted, we'll include template addenda.
[07:37] Elena Park: who owns the evaluation?
[07:39] Diego Morales: Redwood will run the automated pass and create the result sheet; NovaHealth will do a blind manual review of a sampled subset and provide final scoring.
[07:47] Jonas Reed: any blockers on our side? we need to prepare the eval prompts and access to de-identified notes.
[07:52] Maya Patel: legal will expedite the S3 share; expect that by Apr 12.
[07:57] Priya Raman: action items - I'll send benchmark plan and security pack by tomorrow. Diego will prepare shortlist and infra spec.
[08:05] Diego Morales: quick note on evaluation scoring: we'll return per-model triage precision/recall, hallucination list, p95 latency, and cost-per-1M-tokens at the tested config. we'll also surface failure modes.
[08:20] Elena Park: one more thing - can you run a quick adversarial prompt test? clinical hallucinations are the worst.
[08:26] Diego Morales: yes, we'll include a small adversarial set.
[08:29] Elena Park: ok thanks.
[08:31] Priya Raman: any competitors or other vendors you're evaluating?
[08:34] Elena Park: we're running pilots with Anthropic and a closed model provider but want to see open-model economics.
[08:40] Priya Raman: good to know.
[08:42] Diego Morales: final recap, deliverables: 1) benchmark plan + security pack, 2) infra spec + model shortlist + quant configs, 3) benchmark results and recommendation, 4) pilot run.
[08:55] Jonas Reed: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:57] Maya Patel: thanks.
[08:59] Elena Park: thanks, bye.
[09:01] Priya Raman: bye.

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hearings; timestamps approximate. References: security pack (link to redwood security pack), benchmark spreadsheet (we'll share link).
